status: declared by the pull request that closes #426 before any score was computed; nothing here is tuned on a scored day. The setting the pull request flags for Eleonora is announcement_time. Off in every published declaration: no published panel, declaration, record or figure reads it.

inputs.offering: offering_amt, the announced public offering, in USD billions, summed over the auctions of an (issue_date, security_type) group announced by the instant
inputs.maturing: est_pub_held_mat_by_type_amt, the announced estimate of the publicly held securities of that security type maturing on the issue date, in USD billions; one figure per (issue_date, class), the class being the bill types or the coupon types (#566: the figure is one total for every coupon security maturing that day, repeated on each coupon record, so Notes and Bonds share it and subtract it once), taken as the largest non-null figure among the group's auctions announced by the instant; 0.0 when none announced by the instant carries a figure (a cash management bill alone, mostly), counted and reported
inputs.soma: soma_accepted, the Federal Reserve's rollover add-on, is an auction result. It is not in the net: the add-on is sized by the SOMA's own maturing holdings, which the publicly held maturing estimate excludes, so the SOMA leg cancels and the net is the cash the public leg drains. Reported beside the net and reconciled in scripts/net_settlement.py reconcile; dated at the result instant

columns.net_settlement: sum over the settlement groups of the row's own day of (offering - maturing), as announced by the instant, USD billions
columns.net_settlement_bills: the same over the groups whose security_type is a declared bill type (contract.TREASURY_BILL_SECURITY_TYPES)
columns.net_settlement_due_5d: the same net, all security types, summed over the five business days after the row's day (data.next_business_day, the holiday table of metadata/market_holidays.json), as announced by the instant

rule: The value on the panel row of day t is public at 12:00 New York time on t, the declared announcement instant: an auction enters it only when its announcemt_date is on or before t, and its offering and maturing figures are read together, as announced. The forecast made on day t at the 16:00 decision reads the row of day t. A class partly announced on a day (some of its auctions announced by the instant, others settling the same day not yet) is left out of every column until it is fully announced (#679, 13 October 2026): the maturing total covers securities whose offerings were not yet known, so netting it against part of the offering read a cash inflow that was not there (#620), and counting the part with no maturing amount read a drain the unannounced part offsets (#665; scripts/partly_announced_679.py). That more auctions of the class settle that day is read from the auction records of the day as the Treasury's published schedule would show it, and a cash management bill (cash_management_bill_cmb == "Yes") is on no published schedule: it counts toward a class's partial status only from its own announcement, so a cash management bill announced after the instant neither makes the class partial nor enters any figure (#738, Eleonora, 14 October 2026; the earlier reading counted every cash management bill of the day, which reads the future). No unannounced offering or maturing figure enters any column. The first scoring (#426) netted the full maturing amount against the part announced; #620 / #647 counted the announced offerings with no maturing amount.
evidence: Treasury's auction announcements are dated by announcemt_date in the tracked Fiscal Data snapshot, with no clock time. The declared 12:00 rests on Treasury's usual 11:00 a.m. announcement time plus an hour. Treasury's own announcement files state a release time (#1301, metadata/announcement_release_times_1301.json, read on 29 October 2026 from the 3828 announcement files of the snapshot, none unreadable): 3665 state an 'Embargoed Until' time (11:00 for 3535 of them, 08:30 for 117 notes and bonds, 09:30 for 9, 13:30 for 2 bills, 12:50 for 1 cash management bill, 16:15 for 1 note) and 163 say 'for immediate release' with no time (153 cash management bills, 7 bills, 3 notes and bonds). Against the declared 12:00 on announcemt_date: the one file that states a time after the 16:00 decision is a note announced 2019-08-15 that settles 11 weekdays later; three state a time between 12:00 and 16:00 (two bills announced 2018-12-04 at 13:30 and a cash management bill announced 2022-05-17 at 12:50, each settling 5 weekdays later), which the 12:00 instant counts before they were public, though all three were public by the 16:00 decision; the 163 'for immediate release' announcements state no time at all. The 12:00 instant is therefore a declared setting checked against Treasury's files, not a published clock time. At the 16:00 decision any declared instant from 11:00 to 15:59 gives the same sums, so the announcements that could move a sum are the 16:15 file and any 'for immediate release' announcement actually released after the decision, which the files cannot show. A cash management bill is not announced 'the same or the previous day': of the 458 cash management bills settling inside the panel (issue_date from 2018-04-03) in the tracked snapshot, 403 were announced five Monday-to-Friday days before settlement (330 when market holidays, metadata/market_holidays.json, are not counted as days; recounted in the tree for #1327). 2020 (development days, a diagnosis and not a verdict): the net arm's loss against (s3c) is not separable from the immediate-release cash management bills. Target days on which an auction with no stated release time settles carry 67.5% of (s3c-ann-net)'s 2020 grid-CRPS loss (29.4% of (s3c-ann)'s), and with those days left out the net arm's 2020 loss is no longer one (-0.9%, d +0.013 [-0.011, +0.037], undecided); the dating is ruled out as the cause of the flag arm's 2020 loss and not ruled out for the net arm (docs/research/s3c-ann-net-diagnosis-1319-result.md, #1320, Table 4d). repo_model.net_settlement.auction_records refuses a record announced after its auction or after its settlement.

classifiers.hierarchical_logistic: track H (#406): the hierarchical logistic, with the three columns as linear columns
classifiers.onset_logistic: track O (#409, merged as #423): the onset logistic, with the three columns as linear columns
classifiers.not_extended: track Q (#413) is an open pull request, not on main; its models are not extended here
classifiers.why_these_two: They are the classifiers of #406 and #409 that are on main (the directive names #406 and #413; #413 is an open pull request, not main).

hierarchical_logistic_net.base: the hierarchical logistic of track H (#406), repo_model.hierarchical_logistic, features as it declares them at the horizon
hierarchical_logistic_net.added_at_horizons: every horizon: each is public at the declaration's announcement instant on the row's own day, so it is not dropped at h >= 2 as treasury_settlement is
hierarchical_logistic_net.calibration: recalibrated out of fold (pressure.recalibrated), as the control's

onset_logistic_net+recalibrated.base: the onset logistic of track O (#409): kind logistic, no treatment, inputs base and funding of metadata/onset_classifier.json
onset_logistic_net+recalibrated.added_at_horizons: every horizon (treasury_settlement itself still leaves the inputs at h >= 2, as the control's does)
onset_logistic_net+recalibrated.calibration: onset-label fit, then Platt out of fold against the pressure-day outcome (pressure.RECALIBRATION), as the control's

pairing: Each candidate is scored in the same run, on the same scratch panel, folds and horizons as its control (the same classifier without the three columns); the judge's report sets them side by side, and scripts/net_settlement.py pair reports the paired Brier difference with a stationary-bootstrap interval, split by regime and pressure-day type.
